title: Public structs and one error enum that will grow are missing #[non_exhaustive]
description:
Four public items with all-public fields or variants that are certain to grow, none marked `#[non_exhaustive]`, in a workspace where sibling types already use it consistently (Claim, SignedAssertion, FreshnessResult, AttestorError, ConsumerIdentity, TrustBundle, PersonaClaims, IdentityAssurance, PresenceLevel, AssuranceError, AudienceParseError, AttestError all have it):

1. persona-core/src/audience.rs:16-26 `AudienceExtensions` — three public fields. This type exists to carry `persona_*` audience parameters; the parser at audience.rs:60-66 handles exactly two of them today. Any third parameter added later breaks every caller that used a struct literal or an exhaustive `let AudienceExtensions { .. } = ..` destructure.

2. persona-core/src/hvid.rs:7-17 `PresenceInfo` — four public fields, embedded in the already-non_exhaustive `PersonaClaims`. Marking the outer struct and not the inner one leaves the same hole one level down.

3. persona-core/src/spiffe_id.rs:10-23 `SpiffeIdError` — the only error enum in the workspace without it, while `AssuranceError` (assurance.rs:10), `AudienceParseError` (audience.rs:29), `SignerError` (signer.rs:15), `AttestorError` (persona-attestors/src/lib.rs:89) and `AttestError` (persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs:85) all have it. Parsing gains error cases as validation tightens (see the TrustDomain injectivity issue, which needs at least one new variant), and each one is a breaking change today.

4. persona-grpc/src/service.rs:16-20 `WorkloadApiService` — three public fields plus a `new()` taking all three positionally, so both construction paths break on the next field.

All four are free to fix at 0.1.0 and each becomes a semver-major change once anything depends on them. Note the general caveat visible at trust_bundle.rs:18: `#[non_exhaustive]` plus a `new()` that takes every field positionally still breaks callers on a new field — pair it with a builder or Default-based construction where the field count is likely to grow.
